name: Namibian Biltong
description: Biltong, air-dried, vinegar-and-spice-cured meat, is a Namibian staple shared with South Africa - real biltong isn't a smoked or sweetened product, and it's already fully cured and ready to eat.
steps_detailed: Serve the biltong sliced or torn, as-is - it's already fully cured and ready to eat.
steps: Serve the biltong sliced or torn, as-is - it's already fully cured and ready to eat.

name: Namibian Braai-Style Grilled Meat
description: Braai, open-fire grilling, is central to Namibian social eating, shared with the wider Southern African tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and oil.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.
steps: Rub the beef with the garlic and oil.

name: Namibian Oshifima
description: Oshifima, a stiff pearl millet porridge, is a genuine Namibian staple starch, especially in the country's northern Owambo region.
steps_detailed: Whisk the millet and cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes until thick and smooth.

name: Namibian Kapana
description: Kapana, grilled meat sold fresh off the fire at street stalls, is one of Namibia's most beloved street foods.
steps_detailed: Toss the beef with the paprika and oil.
Grill or pan-sear over high heat, turning, 5-6 minutes, until well charred.
steps: Toss the beef with the paprika and oil.

description: Chakalaka, a spicy vegetable relish, is beloved across Namibia as it is throughout Southern Africa.

name: Namibian Mopane Worm-Style Stew
description: Namibia's real mopane worms are a beloved traditional protein source in the country's north - mopane worms aren't a distinct item here, so beef stands in as a widely available protein prepared in a similarly simple, pan-fried style.

name: Namibian Fried Fish

Let rest 15 minutes.
